title: Perceptron & Online Learning
interviewAnswer: The perceptron is an online linear classifier that updates weights only when an example is misclassified. Under linear separability it has a finite mistake bound tied to the margin.
why: The perceptron is a simple foundation for online learning and linear decision rules.
intuition: Process one example at a time: if the current separator is wrong, nudge it toward the correct class.
deepDive: For labels ±1, update w←w+ηyx when y(w·x)≤0. The classical convergence theorem assumes separability; noisy data can cause ongoing updates.
commonMistakes: Confusing perceptron probabilities with logistic regression.
production: Online updates require drift handling, learning-rate/version controls and protection from bad/adversarial labels.
workedExample: A streaming spam classifier can update after each newly labeled message rather than retraining from scratch.
